title: Bank Nifty rebounds over 900 points from day’s low, ends in green as HDFC Bank jumps 2%; PSU banks lag- Moneycontrol.com
text:
My Alerts Go Ad-Free Follow us on: Bank Nifty rebounded more than 900 points from its intraday low to end 0.24 percent higher, led by a 2 percent jump in HDFC Bank as crude oil prices cooled.   September 11, 2026 / 15:52 IST             Bank Nifty staged a sharp turnaround on Friday, rebounding more than 900 points from its intraday low to end in the green, as HDFC Bank and other private-sector lenders gained and crude oil prices retreated sharply from their early highs. The banking index closed 0.24 percent higher at 56,606.55, after falling as much as 1.36 percent earlier in the session to a low of 55,699.45. It finished near the day’s high of 56,645.85. The recovery was in line with a broader rebound in the Indian stock market, although the benchmark indices still ended lower. The Sensex closed down 121 points, or 0.16 percent, at 74,782, but recovered more than 600 points from its intraday low. The Nifty 50 ended 80 points, or 0.34 percent, lower at 23,398, around 170 points above its day’s low. HDFC Bank  emerged as the strongest major contributor to the Bank Nifty recovery, with the stock rising 2.1 percent to Rs 708.25 after hitting an intraday high of Rs 709.  Yes Bank  jumped 5.3 percent to Rs 23.48, while  Kotak Mahindra Bank  gained 0.6 percent to Rs 419. AU Small Finance Bank rose 0.4 percent and Bank of Baroda gained 0.2 percent. However, several banking stocks remained under pressure. IndusInd Bank fell 1.5 percent to Rs 978.20, while SBI declined 1.4 percent to Rs 995.70. IDFC First Bank, Union Bank of India, Canara Bank, Federal Bank and ICICI Bank also ended lower. Private-sector banks outperformed their public-sector peers. The Nifty Private Bank index gained 0.48 percent, while the Nifty PSU Bank index fell 0.62 percent. The broader market also remained weak despite recovering from its intraday lows. The Nifty Midcap 100 fell 0.26 percent and the Nifty Smallcap 100 lost 0.58 percent. Market breadth was negative, with 1,774 shares advancing against 2,372 declining, while INDIA VIX rose 4.1 percent to 12.28. The recovery in Indian equities came as crude oil prices extended their retreat from the day’s highs, easing some of the inflation concerns that had rattled global markets earlier. Brent crude futures fell more than 3 percent to above $104 a barrel, after touching a four-month high of $109.97 earlier on Friday. West Texas Intermediate crude dropped 2.6 percent to near $100 a barrel. US stock-index futures also rebounded as oil prices cooled, although investors remained cautious ahead of the US Consumer Price Index report. The inflation data could further shift expectations for Federal Reserve policy after a slightly hotter-than-expected Producer Price Index reading on Thursday. Despite Friday’s pullback, oil prices remained sharply higher for the week after both Brent and WTI surged more than 6 percent on Thursday. The spike in crude had intensified concerns over inflation and the prospect of further monetary tightening, contributing to the sharp risk-off move across global markets earlier in the session.
